In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BBFK is the best bounded-space on-line bin packing algorithm known.
, in terms of both worst-case performance and average-case performance, BBFK(u) is the best of the known on-line bin packing heuristics for all values of u < 1.

the BBFK algorithms, for all K \in {2,3,4,5}, are the best bounded-space on-line bin packing heuristics known for the problem of packing n items of size s_1, \ldots, s_n into a minimum number of bins, each of which has a unit capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BBFK algorithms are the best of both worlds: they have a worst-case ratio of \frac 7{10} and a running time of O(n), but they also have the best average performance of any bounded-space on-line algorithm.
the Best Fit algorithm is the most efficient of all bounded-space, on- line bin packing algorithms for all but the largest memory bounds.
, for any fixed u, BBFK(u) is a good choice for a bounded-space algorithm, and for u = 1 BBFK is an excellent choice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best-fit strategy is better than the first-fit strategy, even for on-line algorithms that have bounded memory.
the best-fit heuristic, which is known to perform well in practice, can be used effectively in bounded-space on-line algorithms.
, when the goal is to minimize average performance, bounded-space on-line bin packing is not necessarily a bad idea.
